title: Wood blocks, tom-toms and the old Chinese crash cymbal
summary: He describes the percussion accessories used in jazz and the 22-inch Chinese crash cymbal he used on early records, later stolen.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: What all did you use in the way of wood blocks or cowbells and so on?
Well, we used to use all of those things and, uh, tom-toms, the, the old, the old style, not the, not the tunable.

Yeah, the old Chinese. And, uh, and the, the, the, the old Chinese crash was always, for jazz, was always a thing. And then later on, they came out with the Sildjans. And, uh, I never did stop using the crash. And, uh, the, then later on, they put the rivets in the, in the, the old Chinese crash, like the one I, I had when I first recorded with Sharky. For about the first five years. And then, that famous store, I got sick and was laid up for a while and somebody stole it. I never been able to get one with it. Just that right tone. Yeah. It was a, it was a, it was a 22 inch one. Yet, it, but it didn't make too much noise. Wasn't too loud. And it, it didn't ring too, too much. You know, it wouldn't ring over into the next measure. Yeah. Yeah. Oh if you, if you hit it, would just last that, that shh would just last just long enough. So they wouldn't, like these new ones that, these Sildjans things hit, they just keep rolling and rolling. You know. There's no, no distinction in the beats.
